title: Shot Allocation Strategies in Debugging Quantum Circuits
authors: Era Thaqi, Coco Gong, Margaret Martonosi
abstract: Debugging quantum programs remains challenging due to the nature of quantum measurement. As quantum algorithms and systems scale, it is increasingly crucial to develop rigorous debugging and verification approaches. Statistical assertion-based debugging validates quantum program behavior through repeated circuit execution and statistical hypothesis testing, but existing frameworks treat shot count as a fixed input parameter, leaving the problem of optimal shot allocation across multiple mid-circuit assertions unexplored. To improve debugging efficiency by making better use of given shot counts, this paper proposes and evaluates four shot allocation strategies within the QDB quantum debugger implemented within the CUDA-Q framework. These allocation approaches: equal split, static weight allocation, adaptive entropy routing, and sequential retirement, use statistical approaches to test whether qubits have expected state characteristics at different points in execution. We evaluate these allocation strategies on different circuits, under both noise-free and depolarizing noise conditions. We show how adaptive strategies use shots efficiently by concentrating them on assertions with high uncertainty. This substantially reduces total shot usage while maintaining comparable debugging confidence.
summary: This paper addresses the inefficiency of current quantum circuit debugging by proposing advanced shot allocation strategies. It evaluates methods like adaptive entropy routing and sequential retirement, showing they intelligently reallocate limited measurement shots to the most ambiguous parts of the circuit. This significantly boosts debugging confidence while conserving computational resources.
main_problem: The core problem is developing efficient and rigorous debugging and verification methods for quantum programs, specifically optimizing how limited computational resources (shot counts) are allocated across multiple mid-circuit assertions.
main_result: Adaptive shot allocation strategies significantly improve debugging efficiency by concentrating shots on the most uncertain assertions, leading to comparable or better bug detection power with substantially reduced total shot usage.
method: The authors propose and evaluate four distinct shot allocation strategies—including adaptive entropy routing and sequential retirement—within the QDB quantum debugger framework.
model_or_system: The work focuses on debugging quantum circuits executed on a quantum computing platform, utilizing the QDB debugger implemented in the CUDA-Q framework. Debugging relies on statistical assertion-based testing.
key_observables: Shot budget, wasted-shot counts, false positive rates, bug-detection power, and Shannon entropy scores for various assertion types.
important_parameters: Total available shot count (B), and the noise model (noise-free vs. depolarizing noise).
main_assumptions: Existing debugging workflows incorrectly treat the shot count as a fixed input, ignoring the potential for optimal dynamic reallocation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes the performance comparison of the four allocation strategies across multiple quantum circuit benchmarks.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the challenge of shot allocation, details the four proposed strategies ($S_0$ through $S_3$), provides the mathematical basis for entropy scoring, and concludes with evaluations on various circuits under different noise conditions.
why_interesting: While focused on debugging, the concept of dynamically allocating resources based on local uncertainty (entropy) has parallels in adaptive measurement schemes used in characterizing open quantum systems or optimizing quantum control sequences.

Across all benchmarks, S0 wastes the most shots, with waste increasing sharply as the total budget grows. S1 reduces waste by assigning a smaller fixed fraction of the budget to classical assertions, but still behaves similarly to S0.
